html:
The Trundholm sun chariot is a bronze statue of a horse pulling a gilded sun disc on wheels, made in Denmark about 1400 BCE. A farmer ploughed it up from a bog on Zealand in 1902.

One side of the disc is covered in gold and the other is dark, which scholars read as the sun's day and night journeys across the sky. It is the clearest sign of a sun cult in the Nordic Bronze Age, when Denmark traded amber south for bronze and gold.

It had probably been put in the bog on purpose, as an offering, a custom that runs from the Bronze Age to the bog bodies of the Iron Age. It is now a treasure of the National Museum of Denmark and appears on Danish banknotes. See Denmark.
